classification.habitat: Moist shaded places, wetlands and damp grassland
classification.distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions including India

identification.description: Creeping herb with long petioles and characteristic rounded to reniform leaves arising from nodes.
identification.root: Fibrous roots arise from nodes and basal portions.
identification.stem: Slender creeping stolons rooting at nodes.
identification.leaf: Long-petioled, rounded to reniform, shallowly crenate leaves with radiating veins.
identification.flower: Very small pinkish to white flowers in compact clusters near the base of the leaf petiole.
identification.fruit: Small laterally compressed schizocarp-like fruit, splitting into mericarps.

therapeutics.precautions: Do not equate traditional Medhya use with a proven treatment for neurological disease.

major_constituents: Triterpenoid saponins including asiaticoside-type constituents are reported
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Constituent levels vary by plant material and extraction method.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Centella asiatica is widely studied botanically and pharmacologically; this record separates modern evidence from traditional indications.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use authenticated plant material; clinical claims require condition-specific evidence.

mnemonics: Manduka = frog; remember the rounded frog-like leaves and moist habitat
student.quick_revision: Mandukaparni—Centella asiatica; Apiaceae; whole plant; Tikta, Laghu, Sheeta.

discussion_points: Differentiate Mandukaparni from Brahmi/other similarly named Medhya plants.
practical_points: Observe nodes, roots, petiole and leaf venation.

doctor.quick_reference: Traditional Medhya/Rasayana profile; whole plant is used.
key_precautions: Do not substitute another 'Brahmi' species without authentication.
